meta.title: AQAL Platform - Engine Data Handoff for Perplexity
meta.purpose: Unblocks work-order tasks that require the platform's own data. Everything here is the live engine's actual configuration, exported verbatim from the codebase.
meta.integrityRule: Deliverables built on this data still require checked DOIs for every empirical claim. Where you correct one of our numbers, show receipts.

taskUnblockMap.18 edge-case personas: Use taxonomy + engineSamples to see what the engine prescribes per weak line; your own 400-persona format is the base. NOTE: we still need your 400 personas sent back to the platform team for tasks 17/20.
taskUnblockMap.20 scoring QA pack: taxonomy.axes gives the exact 32 line names + scoring modes; questions gives the 27-question order your expected ranges attach to.
taskUnblockMap.22 expand goal templates: goals.templates is the exact schema (key, label, keywords, stages, baselineMonths, minMonthlyHours). Deliver new templates in this shape.
taskUnblockMap.23 science of quitting: goals.clockLogic is the verbatim clock algorithm your disengagement rules must plug into (states, the 'never' rule, pace math).
taskUnblockMap.25 complementarity weights: matching block: current weights, floor, axis subset, and the verbatim scoring function.
taskUnblockMap.27 library sweep 2024-2026: library.clusterSchema + samples show the exact shape new clusters must arrive in.
taskUnblockMap.33 cascade mapping: taxonomy.axes is the canonical node list for your directed cascade edges (fromLine/toLine must use these names).
taskUnblockMap.35 deposit contracts: goals.clockLogic + templates show where stakes would attach (per-goal, per-month logging).
taskUnblockMap.36-40 age/circadian/natural-experiments/: therapyMap + keystones are the intervention universe to annotate; deliver annotations keyed by therapy name / practice id.
taskUnblockMap.42 money pathways: Not actually blocked - pure regulatory research. Pricing context: $449/mo, $4,499/yr, assessments $500-$1,500, first 10,000 free lifetime.

practices.name: Sleep protection
practices.prescription: Protect 7–9h with regular timing — the single highest-leverage move, because sleep gates every other line.
practices.horizon: 2–4 weeks to feel it, ongoing to keep it
practices.researchBasis: Even mild chronic sleep restriction accumulates measurable cognitive and emotional-regulation deficits; restoring it reverses them.

practices.name: Aerobic exercise
practices.prescription: Regular aerobic training (the best-evidenced brain intervention) to lift cognition, mood, and resilience together.
practices.researchBasis: In randomized trials, aerobic training improved memory and executive function and had a large antidepressant effect.

practices.name: Interoception / floatation practice
practices.prescription: Train interoception (breath/body attention, or floatation) — one practice that plausibly lifts self-regulation, empathy, and intuition via the shared insula hub.
practices.researchBasis: Interoceptive training and floatation reliably raise body-awareness and lower anxiety; the insula hub links it to empathy and decision-making.

practices.name: Breathwork / HRV
practices.prescription: Brief daily slow-breathing (e.g. cyclic sighing) to raise vagal tone and improve emotional control and focus.
practices.researchBasis: A randomized trial found five minutes of daily cyclic-sighing beat mindfulness meditation for mood and physiological arousal over a month.

practices.name: Nature exposure
practices.prescription: ~2 hours/week in natural settings to restore attention, lower rumination, and lift mood — passive and low-effort.
practices.researchBasis: A ~2-hour weekly threshold is associated with better health and wellbeing; a single nature walk lowered rumination and its brain signature.

practices.name: Thermal stress (sauna)
practices.prescription: Regular sauna use (strong cohort evidence for brain and cardiovascular healthspan); cold exposure is real acute but over-hyped for durable gains.
practices.researchBasis: Large cohorts link frequent sauna use to substantially lower dementia and cardiovascular mortality (observational).

practices.name: Psychedelic-assisted therapy (documented, not prescribed)
practices.prescription: Documented for durable openness and mood change under strict medical supervision — we DOCUMENT this, we do not prescribe it. Legal, screening, and safety constraints apply.
practices.researchBasis: Supervised psilocybin has produced durable increases in openness and sustained reductions in depression/anxiety in trials — under medical control only.

practices.name: Nonverbal-decoding practice
practices.prescription: Deliberate emotion-reading practice (validated to improve nonverbal decoding). Watching muted interaction is a plausible but UNTESTED exercise — try it, don't bank on it.
practices.horizon: a few weeks of deliberate practice
practices.researchBasis: A meta-analysis found person-perception training reliably improves the accuracy of reading others' nonverbal cues.

practices.name: Watch + discuss relationship media
practices.prescription: With your partner, WATCH and DISCUSS relationship films regularly (the Rogge protocol — halved the 3-year divorce rate; the discussion is the active ingredient).
practices.researchBasis: In a randomized trial, newlyweds who watched and discussed five relationship movies cut their 3-year divorce/separation rate roughly in half (24% → 11%) — matching intensive therapy.

practices.name: Empathy & perspective-taking practice
practices.prescription: Structured perspective-taking practice (imagining the other's experience) — a meta-analysis of RCTs shows empathy is trainable; maintain it with repetition.
practices.researchBasis: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found empathy training produces a moderate, reliable increase in empathy.

practices.name: Communication & conflict skills
practices.prescription: Practice validated communication/conflict-management skills (speaker–listener, repair attempts) — relationship education lowers marital distress, especially with regular practice.
practices.researchBasis: Meta-analyses show relationship education reliably improves couples' communication and lowers marital distress, strongest for higher-risk couples.

practices.name: Parenting-skill practice
practices.prescription: Practice the validated parenting components — warm-and-structured (authoritative) style, emotional communication, positive interaction — WITH your own child (practice beats concepts).
practices.horizon: a program of several weeks, practiced daily
practices.researchBasis: Meta-analyses of parent-training identify the active ingredients (emotional communication, positive interaction, practicing with your own child) that reliably improve child outcomes.

practices.name: Close the knowing–doing gap (implementation science)
practices.librarySection: Knowing vs. Doing — Making It Stick
practices.prescription: Convert every prescription into an if-then plan ('If it's 8pm Tuesday, then we watch our film'), stack it onto an existing habit, and track it. This is the step that turns knowing into doing.
practices.horizon: set up now; ~66 days to automaticity
practices.researchBasis: Implementation intentions (if-then plans) have a medium-to-large effect on actually enacting goals across 90+ studies; habits take a median of ~66 days to form.

practices.name: Automate & escalate saving
practices.prescription: Automate a fixed transfer to savings/investing on payday and pre-commit to escalate it with every raise (the 'Save More Tomorrow' design) so the choice happens once, not monthly.
practices.horizon: set up once; compounds for years
practices.researchBasis: Automatic enrollment and Save-More-Tomorrow escalation dramatically raised real savings rates in field studies by defaulting people into the behavior.

practices.name: Low-cost index investing
practices.prescription: Default to broad, low-fee index funds and hold — most active managers underperform the index net of fees over time, and fees compound against you.
practices.researchBasis: SPIVA and related data show the large majority of active funds underperform their benchmark net of fees over 10–15 year windows.

practices.name: Commitment devices & pre-commitment
practices.prescription: Lock your future self in advance — a commitment savings account, a locked deadline, a stake you forfeit if you slip — so willpower isn't required at the moment of temptation.
practices.horizon: set up now; protects every future decision
practices.researchBasis: Commitment savings accounts (e.g. the SEED trial) and pre-commitment devices meaningfully raised follow-through by removing the in-the-moment choice.

practices.name: Deliberate practice
practices.prescription: Practice at the edge of your ability on the specific sub-skills you're worst at, with immediate feedback and full focus — not comfortable repetition of what you already do well.
practices.horizon: months to years for real mastery
practices.researchBasis: Deliberate practice — focused, feedback-rich reps at the edge of ability — predicts skill gains, though its share of the variance varies by domain (honest: it's a lever, not the whole story).

practices.name: Spaced repetition + retrieval practice
practices.prescription: Learn by testing yourself and spacing the reviews out (not rereading) — retrieval and distributed practice are the two best-replicated ways to make knowledge stick.
practices.researchBasis: The testing effect and distributed practice are among the most robust findings in learning science, repeatedly beating rereading for long-term retention.

practices.name: Deep-work attention blocks
practices.prescription: Protect uninterrupted single-task blocks with the phone out of the room — task-switching carries a real resumption cost, so batching focus beats reacting all day.
practices.researchBasis: Interruption and task-switching research shows measurable resumption-lag costs; the specific 'deep work' protocol is popular but more lightly trialed (honest: Emerging).

practices.name: Behavioral activation
practices.prescription: Schedule small valued or rewarding actions and do them regardless of motivation — action precedes mood here, not the other way around.
practices.researchBasis: Behavioral activation is a first-line, evidence-based treatment for depression, roughly as effective as full CBT in trials.

practices.name: Cognitive restructuring (CBT skills)
practices.prescription: Catch the automatic thought, write it down, and test it against the evidence — the core CBT move that loosens anxious and depressive thinking loops.
practices.researchBasis: CBT is one of the most strongly evidenced psychotherapies for anxiety and depression across hundreds of trials.

practices.name: Resistance training
practices.prescription: Progressive strength training 2–3×/week — it builds muscle and bone, lowers all-cause mortality risk, and has a real antidepressant effect on its own.
practices.researchBasis: Meta-analyses link resistance training to lower all-cause mortality and a moderate reduction in depressive symptoms independent of aerobic exercise.

practices.name: Protein + fiber baseline
practices.prescription: Anchor meals around adequate protein and high fiber — the two dietary levers with the strongest, least-hyped evidence for satiety, muscle, and long-term health.
practices.horizon: weeks for satiety/energy; years for health
practices.researchBasis: Higher dietary fiber shows a strong dose-response link to lower all-cause mortality; adequate protein supports muscle retention and satiety.

practices.name: Invest in social connection
practices.prescription: Protect regular, real, face-to-face contact with people you care about — social connection is one of the strongest predictors of health and longevity there is.
practices.researchBasis: Holt-Lunstad's meta-analyses put weak social connection on par with well-known mortality risks like smoking (honest: observational, but very robust).

practices.name: Anchor a sense of purpose
practices.prescription: Name a purpose bigger than yourself and put one concrete weekly action behind it — a stronger sense of purpose tracks with better health and longevity.
practices.researchBasis: Cohort studies associate a stronger sense of purpose/ikigai with lower mortality and better health (honest: observational, confounding possible).

practices.name: Gratitude & prosocial action
practices.prescription: A brief weekly gratitude reflection plus regular small acts of help — modest but real lifts to wellbeing, and cheap to run.
practices.horizon: weeks; keep it periodic, not daily-forced
practices.researchBasis: Gratitude and kindness interventions produce small-to-moderate wellbeing gains (honest: effect sizes are modest and sensitive to how they're run).

practices.name: Expressive writing
practices.prescription: Write continuously about a stressor for ~15 minutes across a few days — the Pennebaker paradigm helps many people process and get clarity.
practices.researchBasis: Expressive writing produces modest but replicated improvements in processing stressful experiences and some health markers.

practices.name: WOOP / mental contrasting
practices.prescription: Run every goal through WOOP — Wish, Outcome, Obstacle, Plan — pairing the vision with the concrete obstacle and an if-then plan for it, which beats visualizing success alone.
practices.horizon: minutes to set up per goal
practices.researchBasis: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions (WOOP) outperforms indulging in positive fantasy alone for actual goal attainment across trials.

practices.name: Morning light + circadian anchoring
practices.prescription: Get bright light early and keep sleep-wake timing consistent — the cheapest lever for stabilizing circadian rhythm, mood, and daytime energy.
practices.horizon: days to a couple of weeks
practices.researchBasis: Morning bright-light exposure and regular timing reliably phase-anchor circadian rhythm and improve mood and alertness.

practices.name: Structured public speaking (Toastmasters-style)
practices.prescription: Join a weekly speaking club (Toastmasters or equivalent) and deliver one prepared talk a month plus impromptu rounds — the best-evidenced influence-builder there is.
practices.researchBasis: Communication-skills training with live practice and feedback reliably improves persuasion, delivery, and speaking anxiety across many controlled studies.

practices.name: Improv comedy classes
practices.prescription: An 8-week beginner improv course: 'yes-and' under pressure trains wit, adaptability, and social ease faster than anything else that's also this fun.
practices.researchBasis: Improv training studies show gains in divergent thinking, tolerance of uncertainty, and social confidence; humor production is a trainable skill.

practices.name: Group singing / choir
practices.prescription: Join a weekly choir or singing group — no audition needed. Active music-making trains pitch and rhythm while the group trains belonging.
practices.researchBasis: Group singing shows consistent wellbeing, social-bonding, and mood benefits; active music training measurably improves auditory-musical skills at any age.

practices.name: Observational drawing course
practices.prescription: A structured 'learn to see' drawing course (8+ weeks): observational drawing is the most direct trainer of spatial perception and visual judgment.
practices.researchBasis: Drawing instruction produces measurable gains in observational accuracy and spatial representation; aesthetic judgment sharpens with deliberate visual practice.

practices.name: Chess/poker study with post-game review
practices.prescription: Play chess or poker seriously — with the non-negotiable: review every game/session afterward. The review, not the play, is where adversarial thinking is built.
practices.researchBasis: Deliberate game study with error review trains opponent modeling, probabilistic judgment, and calibration; transfer is strongest to structurally similar competitive decisions.

practices.name: Negotiation practice reps
practices.prescription: Run one deliberate negotiation per week — a purchase, a bill, a scheduling conflict — using a named framework (anchoring, calibrated questions, BATNA), and debrief in two sentences.
practices.researchBasis: Negotiation training with practice and feedback shows large skill gains in controlled studies; the skill compounds because opportunities to use it are everywhere.

practices.name: Philosophy reading circle / Socratic practice
practices.prescription: Monthly: one primary text (not commentary) + one discussion — a local philosophy meetup, a Socratic circle, or a serious reading partner. Argue positions you don't hold.
practices.researchBasis: Structured philosophical dialogue programs improve reasoning quality and perspective-taking; wise-reasoning research shows deliberate practice effects.

practices.name: Systems-thinking practice (causal loop mapping)
practices.prescription: Once a week, diagram one real system you're inside — your job's workflow, your family's mornings, your finances — as a causal loop map: stocks, flows, feedback, delays.
practices.researchBasis: Systems-thinking instruction with active modeling improves understanding of feedback and delay dynamics — the core failure mode of untrained planning.

practices.name: Graduated social-confidence practice
practices.prescription: A graduated-exposure ladder for romantic/social confidence: eye contact and small talk daily, one genuine compliment a day, one real conversation with someone new per week — difficulty rising weekly.
practices.researchBasis: Graduated exposure with behavioral practice is the best-evidenced treatment for social anxiety and reliably builds approach confidence; charisma behaviors are trainable.

practices.name: Mentor someone
practices.prescription: Take on one mentee — formally (a program) or informally (a junior colleague, a nephew, a newcomer at your club) — with a standing monthly session.
practices.researchBasis: Mentor-side research shows generativity, purpose, and leadership-skill benefits for the mentor, not just the mentee — teaching is the strongest form of mastery.

strengthChallenges.Logical: Find one decision you're avoiding and write the actual argument for each side — five premises each, then decide.
strengthChallenges.Mathematical: Put numbers on something you've only felt: your real hourly cost of a habit, the compound value of a monthly saving.
strengthChallenges.Spatial: Redesign one physical space you use daily — sketch it, then move three things. Live in the new layout a week.
strengthChallenges.Linguistic: Write a 500-word letter to someone you've been meaning to thank. Send it.
strengthChallenges.Volitional: Pick the task you've dodged longest. Do the first 25 minutes before noon, three days this week.
strengthChallenges.Meta-Cognitive: Predict how three decisions will turn out — write the predictions down. Score yourself at week's end.
strengthChallenges.Intrapersonal: Fifteen minutes, three evenings: write what you actually felt today and what triggered it. No editing.
strengthChallenges.Reflective: Reread something you wrote a year ago. Write one page on who's changed — you or your circumstances.
strengthChallenges.Existential: Write your own obituary the way you hope it reads. Circle the one sentence you're not yet living.
strengthChallenges.Philosophical: Take a belief you hold firmly and argue the opposite for one page — steelman, not strawman.
strengthChallenges.Integrative: Take two unrelated ideas from your week and force a connection: one paragraph on what each teaches the other.
strengthChallenges.Interpersonal: Have one conversation this week where your only job is questions. No stories of your own until they ask.
strengthChallenges.Empathic: Pick someone who frustrated you. Write their side of it so well they'd say 'yes — exactly.'
strengthChallenges.Intuitive: Before three meetings or calls, write one sentence predicting the mood you'll walk into. Check yourself after.
strengthChallenges.Musical: Learn 60 seconds of a song — voice or any instrument. Play it for one human being.
strengthChallenges.Kinesthetic: Learn one physical skill-bite this week: juggle two balls, hold a 60-second plank, land a dance step.
strengthChallenges.Naturalistic: Spend one hour somewhere green with no phone. Name five living things you've never bothered to notice.
strengthChallenges.Strategic: Map one goal three moves deep: your move, the world's likely response, your counter. Write it down.
strengthChallenges.Tactical: Take something you've planned to death and ship the ugly version this week. Done teaches faster than perfect.
strengthChallenges.Adaptive: Break one routine on purpose — new route, new tool, new order. Note what the friction teaches you.
strengthChallenges.Resilient: Do one hard thing you'd normally avoid, then write down: it did not break me. Evidence accumulates.
strengthChallenges.Systematic: Diagram one recurring mess in your life as a system: what feeds it, what it feeds. Find the loop.
strengthChallenges.Architectural: Design something end-to-end on paper this week — a room, a course, a product — every layer labeled.
strengthChallenges.Adversarial: Negotiate one real thing this week — a bill, a price, a deadline. Open with a number. Debrief in two lines.
strengthChallenges.Interoceptive: Three times a day, pause: where is tension sitting in your body right now? Name the spot out loud.
strengthChallenges.Aesthetic: Make one corner of your world deliberately beautiful this week — then notice who else notices.
strengthChallenges.Influence: Pitch one idea to one person this week with a clear ask at the end. Count the yes.
strengthChallenges.Humor: Collect three things that made you laugh this week and retell one — landing a laugh is a rep.
strengthChallenges.Parenting: Give someone younger 30 undistracted minutes: their agenda, your full attention, zero advice unless asked.
strengthChallenges.Seduction: Give three genuine, specific compliments to three different people this week. Specific beats smooth.
strengthChallenges.Community-Founding: Gather people once this week — a dinner, a game, a walk. You call it, you host it.
strengthChallenges.Financial-Self-Management: Automate one money move this week — a transfer, a payment, a rule — so future-you can't forget it.

samples.title: Which Weakness Controls the Others — Network Centrality
samples.conclusion: Traits behave as a web of mutually reinforcing nodes, not symptoms of one hidden cause. The most central node — highest expected influence — is the one whose change ripples furthest through the rest. This is the rigorous form of “which weakness has the most controlling influence over the others.” Honest boundary: what centrality means in psychological networks is actively debated, so we treat “your most central weakness” as a model-based hypothesis to confirm on our own cohort, not a settled fact.

samples.title: The Weakest Link Caps the Whole — Bottleneck & O-Ring
samples.conclusion: A profile is not the average of its lines — a single deficiency can cap the whole outcome no matter how strong the rest. Liebig's Law of the Minimum (growth limited by the scarcest input) and Kremer's O-Ring theory (one faulty component ruins the finished product) are the rigorous forms of “your weakest cluster sinks your best strengths.” This is why weakness-shielding, not just strength-maximizing, is core to the platform.

samples.title: One Strength Lifts the Rest — Mutualism & Keystone Effects
samples.conclusion: Strengths don't just co-occur — they pull each other up. The mutualism model shows cognitive abilities reciprocally reinforce each other in development (why strong minds tend to be broadly strong), and “keystone” research shows a single sustained habit spilling over into unrelated domains. Together: sharpening the right strength can raise the entire profile.

samples.title: Where to Intervene, and How to Hold It — Leverage Points & Tracking
samples.conclusion: Not all interventions are equal — a few nodes are high-leverage (a small change moves everything), most are not. Meadows' leverage-points hierarchy is the map for choosing which node to enhance or deplete. And implementation-intention research (if-then plans) is the evidence base for the tracking that keeps a targeted weakness from unconsciously derailing goals.

samples.title: Complementary Matching — Collective Intelligence
samples.conclusion: The network reaches past one person: a partner whose strengths cover your blind spots measurably raises joint performance. The collective-intelligence “c factor” shows group ability depends on composition and social sensitivity, not just individual IQ. Honest boundary: diversity helps on an inverted-U — too much hurts coordination — so matching is tuned, not maximized.

samples.title: Strength & Resistance Training
samples.conclusion: Resistance training is among the most robustly evidenced levers for longevity and daily function, and it builds the volitional follow-through that sits downstream of every other line. Bolsters clusters: body-disconnect, burnout-pattern, imposter-complex.
